screened.motion: This house believes a coding agent should never be allowed to edit monitoring, logging or alerting code.
screened.why: Both reject the blanket "never" as too blunt and converge on the same position: agents may work on ordinary logging code but must never weaken oversight of themselves without explicit human approval enforced outside the agent.

screened.motion: This house believes a vulnerability found with AI should be published with a working exploit on the day the patch ships.
screened.why: Both oppose the motion: Claude, though assigned the against side, would rather delay the full exploit for a short time, and Gemini, though assigned the for side, calls day-one exploit drops reckless.

why: Neither the pick nor the backup split the agents in their private openings.
